I am a microbial ecologist working as a postdoctoral researcher in
Gabriele Micali's Microbial Ecology Lab at
[IRCCS Humanitas Research Hospital](https://www.humanitas.net/) in Milan.
I study how bacteria grow and interact — how cross-feeding, cooperation and
cheating shape the composition of small communities, and how those interactions
change the way populations respond to antibiotics.

My work sits between the bench and the terminal: I run growth experiments in
plate readers, microfluidic chambers and continuous-culture bioreactors, and I
write the analysis pipelines that turn those time-series into growth rates,
lineages and dose–response curves. Most of that code is open — see
[Software](software.qmd).

I did my doctoral research in microbial ecology at Friedrich Schiller
University Jena and the German Centre for Integrative Biodiversity Research
(iDiv), where I tested ecological theory with synthetic bacterial communities and models of
public-goods "cheating". Before that I trained in ecology and evolution at
Imperial College London and in biology at the University of Hull.

## Interests

- Microbial interactions: cross-feeding, public goods, cooperation and cheating
- Bacterial growth dynamics and antibiotic tolerance
- Quantitative methods for growth-curve, timelapse and bioreactor data
- Open, reproducible analysis tooling in R and Python
